title: Christmas Toffee
source: From Karen Massimino  ·  Christmas and holiday gift-giving
headnote: Karen Massimino makes this toffee every Christmas season — about eight batches at once — and it goes out as holiday gifts.

items.raw: 2 tablespoons water (helps keep it from separating)
1 cup (about 120 g) chopped almonds, pecans, or walnuts, toasted

steps.text: Line a 10×15-inch rimmed baking sheet with parchment or a silicone mat. Toast the nuts in a dry skillet until fragrant, then chop. Measure the vanilla and chocolate and have them next to the stove — once the toffee is ready there is no time to look for anything.
In a heavy 3-quart saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the sugar, water, and salt and stir until the sugar dissolves.

Clip on a candy thermometer and keep stirring with a wooden spoon or heatproof spatula, scraping the bottom, as it boils. It will turn from pale yellow to the color of peanut butter and then a light amber. Stop at exactly 300°F (hard crack), which takes 15 to 20 minutes.

steps.lead: Off the heat, add the vanilla.
steps.text: Pull the pan off the burner and stir in the vanilla. It will sputter. Vanilla goes in now, not at the start — at 300°F the flavor cooks away.
Immediately pour onto the prepared sheet and spread with the spatula into a thin, even layer, about ⅛ inch thick. It sets within a minute, so move quickly.

Wait 1 to 2 minutes, then scatter the chocolate chips over the hot toffee. Let them sit 3 to 5 minutes to melt, then spread into an even layer. Sprinkle the nuts over the top and press them in lightly.
Let cool at room temperature about 2 hours, or 30 minutes in the refrigerator once it is no longer hot, until the chocolate is firm. Break into pieces.

notes.label: If it separates
notes.text: if a layer of butter pools on top, pull the pan off the heat, add a tablespoon or two of hot water, and stir hard until it comes back together. Then return it to the heat. Sudden heat changes and not stirring are the usual causes.

notes.label: Karen makes about eight batches
notes.text: make them one at a time. Doubling in one pot cooks unevenly and is much more likely to separate.

notes.label: Check the thermometer
notes.text: it should read 212°F in boiling water. If it reads differently, adjust the 300°F target by the same amount.

notes.label: Storage
notes.text: airtight at room temperature for 2 weeks, layered with parchment. Keep it away from humidity, which makes it sticky.
